# Corpus Mining: Benebell Wen, *I Ching, The Oracle* (North Atlantic Books, 2023)

Source PDF: `/mnt/agents/upload/_OceanofPDF.com_I_Ching_the_Oracle_-_Benebell_Wen.pdf` (1178 PDF pages).
Page citations below are **printed book pages**, approximated from PDF page minus ~68 (calibrated against Wen's own index: Earth trigram section = printed pp. 222–225). Treat page numbers as ±2. Chapter/table numbers are exact.

## 1. SMALLEST FRAGMENTS (primitives inventory)

| # | Fragment | Definition / evidence |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| F1 | **Yin (陰) / Yang (陽)** | "the smallest of metaphysical units in Taoist cosmology… subatomic particles where yin is a negative charge and yang is a positive charge" (ch. 5, ~p. 178). Full polarity table (Table 5-2): Yin = dark, curved, spirit realm, night, wet, moon, cold, restraint, contracting, yielding, passive, autumn, winter, even numbers, intuition, electron, estrogen, mercy, esoteric, receiving hand, northern/shaded side of hill. Yang = light, straight, sentient realm, day, dry, sun, hot, action, expanding, forceful, active, spring, summer, odd numbers, logic, proton, androgen, justice, exoteric, giving hand, southern/sunny side. |
| F2 | **Four Faces of God (四象 Sì Xiàng)** | Four combinations of yin/yang pairing: Elder yin 太陰, Younger yang 少陽, Younger yin 少陰, Elder yang 太陽 (Table 5-4, ~p. 181). Elder = self-paired (fixed/matured); Younger = opposite-paired (changing). Generation rule: each Face "mates with" yin or yang to produce trigrams. |
| F3 | **Trigram (gua 卦)** | Three-line figure; "eight triplicities from which all matter is constructed" (ch. 5). Fuxi ordinal numbering: 1 Heaven 乾, 2 Lake 兌, 3 Fire 離, 4 Thunder 震, 5 Wind 巽, 6 Water 坎, 7 Mountain 艮, 8 Earth 坤 (Tables 4-11, 7-5). |
| F4 | **Yao (爻) line + line-place** | Six places bottom→top; odd positions (1,3,5) innately yang, even (2,4,6) innately yin. Line titles: 初九/九二… (9 = yang), 初六/六二… (6 = yin) (ch. 8 Preliminary Notes, ~p. 489). |
| F5 | **Numbers 6/7/8/9** | Sum of three yarrow counts: 6 = changing yin (X), 7 = unchanging yang, 8 = unchanging yin, 9 = changing yang (X). Mapping to Faces: 6 = Younger yin 少陰?? — note Wen's own Table 7-2 labels: 6→changing yin, 7→Elder yang (unchanging yang), 8→Elder yin (unchanging yin), 9→Younger yang (changing yang) [Wen swaps the conventional elder/younger glosses; flagged in Table 7-2, ~p. 363] [uncertain: her Face labels vs. standard]. |
| F6 | **Hexagram (gua)** | Two stacked trigrams; lower trigram = human/physical/foundation; upper trigram = Spirit/karmic/Heaven's Will (Summary Outline, ch. 7, ~p. 463). |
| F7 | **Nuclear / structural transforms** | Changing lines produce transformed hexagram (Gua Bian 卦變); pairs in King Wen sequence are vertical flips or yin-yang polarities (ch. 8, ~p. 492). |
| F8 | **Wu Xing 五行 (Five Phases)** | Wood 木, Fire 火, Earth 土, Metal 金, Water 水. "Wǔ means 'five' and xíng means 'movement'" — five phases of change, not elements; they are "agents of change" catalyzing trigram transformation (ch. 6, ~p. 306). Earliest source: Book of Documents: "The first is Water, the second is Fire, the third is Wood, the fourth is Metal, the fifth is Earth… Water is the dampness moving downward, Fire is the rising flame, Wood is the straight column, Metal will reform and expel, Earth is the sowing…" (~p. 306). |
| F9 | **Taiji 太極 / Wuji 無極** | Numinous omnipresence (Light) / numinous void; the One that divides into Two. Jí 極 also = North Star, "mythical center of the universe" (ch. 5, ~p. 190). |
| F10 | **Creation vs Completion numbers (Hé Tú)** | Table 5-9: numbers 1–5 = creation (yang), 6–10 = completion (yin); each maps to binary, wuxing, Fuxi direction, King Wen direction (see C6 below). |
| F11 | **Heavenly Stems 干 (10) / Earthly Branches 支 (12)** | Sexagenary cycle of 60; stems pair yin/yang × 5 phases; branches pair zodiac animals, double-hours, months (Appendix B, ~p. 1022; Tables 7-8, 7-9). |
| F12 | **Qi 氣** | Charges of yin/yang; "fueling the changes of yin and yang qi are the Wu Xing" (ch. 6). |

### C2. Trigram ↔ Western elements ↔ Wu Xing ↔ Four Faces (Table 5-1, ~p. 177)
Fire(Western, active) ↔ Younger yang ↔ Fire trigram + Thunder/Wind (Wood); Water(Western, passive) ↔ Younger yin ↔ Water trigram; Air(active) ↔ Elder yang ↔ Heaven; Earth(passive) ↔ Elder yin ↔ Earth trigram; key row also assigns Lake & Mountain. Full: Fire=Lí(Fire)/Thunder,Wind(Wood); Water=Kǎn(Water); Air=Qián(Metal); Earth=Kūn(Earth) — with Duì=Metal, Gěn=Earth under "key yin".

Lo Shu: 4 9 2 / 3 5 7 / 8 1 6 (all rows/cols/diagonals = 15; "fifteen… signifies balance of the trinities", ch. 5). Superimposed on King Wen's Later Heaven Ba Gua: 1=Water(N), 2=Earth(SW), 3=Thunder(E), 4=Wind(SE), 5=center(no trigram), 6=Heaven(NW), 7=Lake(W), 8=Mountain(NE), 9=Fire(S). ### C6. Wu Xing cycles (rules of alchemy, ch. 6, ~p. 320)
- **Creation cycle 相生**: Wood→Fire→Earth→Metal→Water→Wood (circle).
- **Destruction cycle 相克**: Wood breaks Earth, Earth breaks Water, Water breaks Fire, Fire breaks Metal, Metal breaks Wood (pentagram).
- Mozi caveat: quantity/mass can override the cycle ("Metal can defeat Fire if its quantity and mass are large enough").
- Three main rules per phase: what nourishes it / what it controls (subdues) / what weakens it (yields to); plus "created by" and "exhausts".

### C7. Wu Xing ↔ Four Faces ↔ trigram phase-transitions (Tables 6-1, 6-2, 6-3, 6-5; ~pp. 308–312)
Yin changes via Metal (younger yin → Heaven/Lake; West, autumn, Venus, harvest) and Water (elder yin → Water; North, winter, Mercury, contract/retreat). Yang changes via Wood (younger yang → Thunder/Wind; East, spring, Jupiter, growth) and Fire (elder yang → Fire; South, summer, Mars, expand). Equilibrium = Earth (Earth/Mountain; Center, Saturn). "Heaven changes into Lake when the agent of change is Metal. Heaven changes into Water when the agent of change is Water" (~p. 312). Weekday naming: Tuesday Fire, Wednesday Water, Thursday Wood, Friday Metal, Saturday Earth.

### C8. Wu Xing ↔ Five Heads of State (Table 6-7, Dong Zhongshu): Wood=Minister of agriculture; Fire=Minister of war; Earth=Sovereign; Metal=Minister of education; Water=Minister of justice.

## 3. RULES

### R1. Yarrow stalk method (Ten Wings / Xici, per Zhu Xi's 1188 reconstruction; ch. 7, pp. 354–368)
1. 50 stalks; set down 1 vertical (the unused stalk = Nonbeing/wu) while invoking Divinity and stating the inquiry.
2. Divide remaining 49 into two bundles (separation into yin/yang; Creation reenactment). Place one bundle atop the vertical stalk = connecting Heaven; set the other at bottom = Earth.
3. Take 1 stalk from Earth bundle, hold between pinky and ring finger = the diviner's qi connecting Heaven and Earth.
4. Count Earth bundle in groups of 4 (= four directions/seasons = space & time); remainder (4,3,2,1) between ring and middle fingers.
5. Count Heaven bundle in 4s; remainder likewise. Count 1 yields 5 or 9 stalks total: 5→record 3 (qi is Earth/Wu Xing), 9→record 2 (qi is Heaven).
6. Repeat entire process for Count 2 and Count 3 (each yields 4 or 8: 4→record 3, 8→record 2).
7. Sum of three counts: 6 = changing yin (X), 7 = unchanging yang, 8 = unchanging yin, 9 = changing yang (X) (Tables 7-1, 7-2).
8. Six repetitions build the hexagram bottom-up; mark changing lines; flip them for the transformed hexagram.
Stalks stored wrapped in scented silk in a black pouch (= wu wei, the One), in a bamboo/wood tube on the north side of the altar; daily incense maintains qi.

### R2. Coin toss (ch. 7, ~p. 385; history: pre-AD 200, Wang Bi commentaries; popular Tang)
- Three coins tossed six times, bottom-up. Two traditions conflict: Image & Number = three-of-a-kind → fixed lines; **Meaning & Principle (Wen's choice): 3 heads = changing yang, 3 tails = changing yin, 2H1T = fixed yang, 2T1H = fixed yin** (Tables 7-3, 7-4). Coin symbolism: circle=Heaven, square hole=Earth ("circling the square" embedded in the tool).
- Legge's simplified method (Table 5-16) noted historically.

### R3. Reading the cast field (Wen's protocol, ~p. 393)
1. Primary hexagram Oracle text = summary/thesis of situation.
2. Changing lines of primary = practical advice / forecasts on current variables.
3. Transformed hexagram = if-then statement (what happens if advice unheeded).
4. Changing lines of transformed = parting words.
Scope of reading: primary Oracle + its changing lines (+ optionally all six lines) + transformed Oracle + its changed lines.

### R4. Locked hexagram rule
No changing lines = locked hexagram: "all possible variables… have already revealed themselves… the outcome is immutable"; alternatively "internal energies in flux, causing stasis… something within must be unblocked first" (~p. 395). Read all six lines chronologically (L1=past→L6=forecast); line 5 (hexagram ruler) is the crux/answer; line 6 = spiritual guidance.

### R5. Multiple changing lines
One changing line = straightforward solution. "Three or more changing lines: the situation right now is quite volatile… uncertainty, due in large part to your own indecisiveness" (Summary Outline, ~p. 465). If-then pairing: primary changing line = "if"; same line number in transformed hexagram = "then."

### R6. Preparations & ritual grammar (ch. 7, pp. 348–354)
- Dedicated room along north side, entrance facing south; approach table from east, leave west (sun's path).
- Clean table, burn 3 incense sticks; wash hands, rinse mouth (Shinto harae); read sutras first (Buddhist); dress respectfully.
- Invocation restates cosmology: "I call upon the Taiji, the numinous Light, the Wuji, the numinous stillness of Being. I call upon the affinity of the sun and the moon, and the four faces of the holy Spirit, and who, through the five mysteries of change, produce the eight divine revelations…" (full text ~p. 351).
- Wen's personal invocation of Jiǔ Tiān Xuán Nǚ, Lady of the Nine Heavens ("lend me the spirit and power of your sword, and the spirit and power of your gourd…").

### R7. Plum Blossom numerology methods (Shao Yong; ch. 4 & 7)
- Rice-grain casting: count handful, divide by 8, remainder → trigram number (remainder 0 → 8 Earth); first pile = lower trigram, second = upper (Table 7-5).
- Calendar/horary formulas (Table 7-7): Upper trigram = (Month+Day+Year)/8 remainder; Lower = (Month+Day+Year+Hour)/8; Changing line = (Month+Day+Year+Hour)/6 remainder. Dates must be converted to lunisolar calendar; year = sexagenary number 1–60; hour = branch number 1–12.
- Whole-number rule: "11 + 24, not 1+1+2+4… 1+1 under this system is an entirely different variable from 11."
- Repeating numbers in a casting = the Tao speaking (synchronicity validation).
- Birth-date method: (month+day+year)/5 remainder → Wu Xing → Five Mystical Arts affinity (Practicum 6.2). Bibliomancy variant: random page number / 8.

### R8. Interpretive layering rules
- Lower trigram = people/human factor/foundation; upper = Spirit/Heaven's Will; transformed upper trigram's Wu Xing = the action to take in spellcraft/petition (Summary Outline).
- Innate line-position qi (odd=yang, even=yin) compared with actual line: match = elder (stable), mismatch = younger (changing energy) (Table 4-2).
- Image & Number tradition = predictive alchemy via correspondences; Meaning & Principle = moral/rational principle extraction (Wang Bi: "the Oracle never takes away your agency"). One of six lines holds the hexagram's core principle/lǐ; the other five are supporting cast.
- Hexagram pairing logic of King Wen sequence: pairs are vertical flips; boundary pairs (1/2, 27/28, 29/30, 61/62, 63/64) are yin-yang polarities; 63/64 are both (~p. 492).

### R9. Spellcraft rules (ch. 3, Tables 3-12, 3-13)
- Eight doubled-trigram hexagrams (1, 58, 30, 51, 57, 29, 52, 2) = Eight Spirit Helpers with programmable functions (e.g., 57 = steady profit; 29 = shamanic journeying; 2 = fertility/mediumship).
- Hexagram spell: approach table from south facing north; draw lines bottom-up; odd lines drawn with thrusting yang assertion, even lines with soft yin reception; six incantation prompts bottom-up: (1) invocation prayer, (2) state problem specifically, (3) declare desired outcome, (4) state secondary concern, (5) declare problem will be resolved, (6) gratitude. Seal with personal stamp + "Jí ji rú lǜ lìng 急急如律令" (= "So mote it be").

### R10. Way of the Sages — four levels of study (Sima Qian, ch. 3): (1) read as literature; (2) reconcile conduct with counsel; (3) counsel state/community (exoteric); (4) [esoteric mastery — implied continuation].

## 4. SYNTAX / STRATA

### S1. Textual layers (ch. 8 Preliminary Notes, ~p. 489)
- **Zhouyi (Basic Classic 本經)**: 64 hexagram figures 卦; two scrolls (Hex 1–30, 31–64); yao lines 爻; hexagram names 卦名; Judgments/Oracle statements 卦辭 (attributed to King Wen); line statements 爻辭 (attributed to Duke of Zhou).
- **Ten Wings** (attributed to Confucius): Wen translates the image statements 象曰 (xiàng yuē) with each hexagram; Xici 繫辭傳 (Great Treatise I & II) = source of yarrow method; Shuo Gua 說卦 (Eighth Wing) = source of trigram correspondences & Eight Spirit Helpers.
- Line titles formula: 初九 chū jiǔ (first 9 = yang L1), 九二 (yang L2)… 六二 (yin L2)… 用九/用六 (special "all lines changing" texts exist for Hexagrams 1 and 2 — Wen includes "The Changing Sixth Line" Great Change text, ~p. 502).

### S2. Formulaic divination phrases with valence (ch. 8 notes, pp. 495–500; ch. 2 ~p. 74)
| Phrase | Valence / gloss |
|---|---|
| 元亨利貞 yuán hēng lì zhēn | Confucian four virtues: "to be perfected, to be accomplished, to always advance, and to always persevere." Original Zhou meaning of 貞 zhēn = "to divine, holding ritual offerings"; 亨 hēng = ritual sacrifice + obtaining the god's answer. |
| 吉 jí | Auspicious, good fortune (fortuitous omen). |
| 凶 xiōng | Ominous; misfortune "beyond your control or after a long chain of karmic consequences." |
| 無咎 wú jiù | "There is no blame" — neutral state; errors made but no harm/karma; Xici: indicates rectification of errors; "it is what it is." 咎 jiù also connotes metameleia (regret/self-condemnation). |
| 吝 lìn | "Endeavor for corrective measures" (Legge: "regret"; Wilhelm: "humiliation") — preventable misfortune caused by one's own petty personality; a warning, still within control. |
| 利涉大川 lì shè dà chuān | "Crossing the great stream" — be bold, undertake the great hazardous enterprise (historically: King Wu crossing the Yellow River, 1122 BC); negative form 不利涉大川 = prepare more first. |
| 有求必應 yǒu qiú bì yìng | "If there is a request, it shall be answered" (Qianlong-era inscription reproduced with Hexagram 1). |
| 悔 / 厲 | regret / danger (appear in line texts, e.g., Hex 1 L6 有悔 "will repent"). |

### S3. Alternative sequences
King Wen received order (authoritative; mythic channeling c. 1050 BC); Mawangdui order (168 BC silk MS; Table 3-5: Mawangdui 1–8 = King Wen 1, 12, 33, 10, 6, 13, 25, 44); Fuxi order (Shao Yong, 11th c. AD).

## 5. CANDIDATE DIMENSION ATTRIBUTION (Wen corpus)

Dimensions: **Movement** (vectors/where) · **Evolution** (becoming/when) · **Being** (state/quality) · **Design** (structure/form) · **Space** (container/resonance)

| Fragment / class | Proposed dimension | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Yin/yang charges (F1) | Being | intrinsic qualities/states; polarity table of attributes |
| Four Faces (F2) | Evolution | defined by generation dynamics (elder=fixed, younger=changing); map to alchemical stages nigredo→rubedo (C23) |
| Trigram attribute lists (C1) | Being (quality) + Movement (direction) | mixed: qi-quality/body/sound = Being; direction/hours = Movement; ritual tool = Design? |
| Hexagram figure + line places (F4, F6, C26) | Design | pure structural positions; feudal hierarchies, narrative arc = form grammar |
| Changing lines 6/9 (F5) | Evolution | operators that transform one state into another |
| Wu Xing phases + cycles (F8, C6, C7) | Evolution | explicitly "phases of change," generation/conquest cycles = transformation rules |
| Hé Tú / Lo Shu numbers (C3, C4) | Design (Lo Shu = applied structure) + Space (Hé Tú = innate flow map) | Wen: Hé Tú = innate flow; Lo Shu = "applied sciences for controlling that flow" |
| Directions/compass (C1, C13–C16) | Movement/Space | directions are vector space; Wen's mandala = "compass and atlas" |
| Solar terms, months, Shao Yong time categories (C13–C15, C27) | Evolution (when) | calendric cycles, epochs, 360-year revolutions |
| Stems & branches (F11, C11–C12) | Evolution + Being | cyclic time markers carrying phase qualities |
| Sound correspondences (C1 Sound field) | Space (resonance) | drumbeat/chimes/silence as environmental resonance of each trigram |
| Tarot/Qabalah/DNA cross-maps (C18–C25) | Design | structural isomorphisms between systems (binary code, 8×8 grids) |
| Formulaic omen phrases (S2) | Being + Evolution | valence states assigned to situations; 吝 = still-changeable, 凶 = karmically fixed |
| Locked hexagram (R4) | Being (stasis) | no transformation operators active |
| Ritual space rules (R6) | Space | consecrated container; north-side altar, east approach |

## 6. BIGGEST FINDINGS (Wen)

1. **Complete 8×20 trigram correspondence matrix** (C1) — directions, planets, zodiac, moon phases, hours, sounds, body, tools, animals, immortals — the richest single primitive-to-attribute system in the corpus.
2. **Wen's original tarot↔trigram system with the phantom 9th gua Xuán (玄, the Void)** (C20–C21): 72/78 cards mapped to 8 trigrams; six "Spirit Helper" majors mapped to six physics laws (Newton ×3, Faraday, Schrödinger, mass-energy); double-※ = 65th hexagram. Directly relevant to extending a state space beyond 64.
3. **Dual solar-term systems** (C15): "Natural Cycle" vs. "Thaumaturge's Taiji" — an explicit rule that operative correspondences invert natural ones to achieve balance (a control-system rule, not just a map).
4. **Yarrow stalk numerics fully specified** (R1) with cosmological justification for every gesture (50→49→2→4; 5/9, 4/8; sums 6/7/8/9).
5. **Wu Xing altar tables** (C5) give a 5×25+ correspondence block (color, taste, sense, organ, tissue, finger, brain function, chemical class, grain, gem, metal, livestock, Confucian relation, life phase, alchemical process, mystical art, totem, planet, time, virtue).
